title: Wangusi v. Amazon Web Services & Virginia Connects
jurisdiction: Circuit Court of Arlington County, VA (CL26002535-00)
parties: Dr Nathan Wangusi (former AWS water sustainability manager) v. AWS; Virginia Connects
claims_challenged: AWS: NoVA "dropped water use by 42 percent"; "75 percent of the way to water positive"; facilities run "ninety-seven percent of the year… not using any water". Alleges Virginia Connects ran a coordinated video campaign the same day.
status: Pending; jury trial sought. AWS declined to comment; says its water data were third-party assured.

title: 16-state AG investigation into '100% renewable' claims
claims_challenged: Claims to be '100% renewable' / 'powered by renewable energy' based on unbundled renewable energy certificates (RECs).
status: Inquiry letters (responses were due Oct 27, 2025); no public findings reported as of Oct 2026.

title: Amazon 'AWS Water Positive Public Launch' memo
claims_challenged: 2022 memo planning the 'water positive' campaign warned transparency was "a one-way door" and advised keeping projections confidential; indirect water (~90% of footprint) left out.

title: The Roanoke Rambler v. Western Virginia Water Authority
parties: The Roanoke Rambler (news outlet) v. Western Virginia Water Authority (re Google, Botetourt Co.)
claims_challenged: Sought disclosure of Google's planned water use; Google's announcement centred on 'water stewardship'.
status: A judge ordered the records released; contracts show 2 million gallons/day, up to 8 million with expansion. The Authority sought an appellate stay.

title: Milwaukee Riverkeeper v. City of Racine
parties: Midwest Environmental Advocates for Milwaukee Riverkeeper v. City of Racine (re Microsoft Mount Pleasant)
claims_challenged: Alleges public-records violations over Microsoft data center water use.
status: Racine released the records Sep 17, 2025 (Phase 1 ~2.8M gal/yr; up to 8.4M gal/yr later). Case outcome not reported.

title: Municipality of Cerrillos v. Google data center
parties: Municipality of Cerrillos, residents v. Google
claims_challenged: Projected 169 litres/second of water for cooling; climate impacts on water supply not assessed.
status: Permit partially annulled (Feb 2024); Google withdrew the original groundwater-cooled design and is redesigning with air cooling.

title: ClientEarth, FIE & Friends of the Earth Ireland v. CRU (Ireland), in LSE climate-litigation report
parties: ClientEarth, Friends of the Irish Environment, Friends of the Earth Ireland v. Commission for Regulation of Utilities
claims_challenged: The regulator's Large Energy Users Connection Policy for data centres; energy and climate impacts not properly assessed.
status: High Court leave granted Apr 28, 2026; pending. Highlighted in the LSE Grantham 2026 litigation report (Jun 2026).

title: Foxglove & Global Action Plan v. UK government (Woodlands Park, Iver)
parties: Foxglove, Global Action Plan v. Secretary of State
claims_challenged: Energy use of the data centre not considered.
status: In Jan 2026 the government conceded a 'serious logical error' (the promised low-carbon mitigation could not be secured) and said permission should be quashed. JR permission granted Jan 22, 2026; developer still contests; no final order reported.

title: NM State Ethics Commission: Project Jupiter ad campaign
claims_challenged: Oracle reported $3,444,500 paid to Brabender Cox for the ad campaign; the Commission treated the ads as lobbying aimed at the state's air-permit review.
status: Commission calls it likely the largest lobbying advertising campaign ever disclosed in New Mexico.
